To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children with more letter knowledge are quicker to look at and spend more time looking at print, and they look at the first letter of a word more than do children with less letter knowledge.
children attended little to the text, took longer to fixate the print than the illustrations, and labeled less than half the letters.
children who knew more letters were quicker at looking at the letters in a book and spent more time attending to the letter, the word and its first letter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of reading in children and the role of eye movement in the development of reading.
the role of letter names and letter-sound knowledge in children's reading of alphabet books.
how children's knowledge of the alphabet and the ability to read words develop in conjunction with each other.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the children were able to recognize the letters in the book but did not use them in the word recognition process.
the eye movement study showed that children attending little to the print took longer to first fixation print than illustration and labeled less letters than when presented in isolation.
the children were not attending to print in an alphabetic way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
letter knowledge and alphabet book reading may facilitate children’s entrance into the alphabetic phase of reading.
the children in our study were at the beginning of the transition from the logographic stage to the partial alphabetic phase of reading development.
the eye movements of children reading alphabet books are influenced by letter knowledge and the print and picture features on the page.
The main takeaway from our work is that

letter knowledge is a necessary but not a sufficient condition for the ability to read an alphabet book and that the eye movement patterns of the children were consistent with the idea that letter knowledge was related to the ability to recognize words in an alphabet book.
children's eye movements are influenced by the print and the pictures on a page, but the print is not the focus of attention in the way it is in older children.
children’s letter knowledge is a key factor in their ability to attend to print in alphabet books.
